earnings_release.text: EX-99.1 2 exhibit991enrschedules3q26.htm EX-99.1 Document Exhibit 99.1 October 22, 2026 Dow reports third quarter 2026 results FINANCIAL HIGHLIGHTS • Net sales were $11.3 billion, up 13% year-over-year, reflecting increases in all operating segments. • Local price increased 14% versus the year-ago period, led by gains in Packaging & Specialty Plastics, with higher polyethylene prices in all regions. Currency was flat year-over-year. • Volume decreased 1% year-over-year. This reflects higher volumes in all regions except Asia Pacific, where impacts from the Middle East conflict are most pronounced. • GAAP net income was $525 million. Operating EBIT 1 was $887 million, up $707 million year-over-year, primarily driven by higher prices as well as benefits from the Company’s collective self-help actions, which more than offset higher raw materials and logistics costs. • GAAP earnings per share (EPS) was $0.62; operating EPS 1 was $0.71, compared to a loss of $0.19 in the year-ago period. Op. EPS excludes significant items totaling $0.09 per share, primarily driven by costs associated with the Company’s collective self-help actions. • Cash provided by operating activities – continuing operations was $1.8 billion, up $709 million year-over-year, reflecting improved earnings and working capital, and up $515 million sequentially, primarily reflecting working capital improvements. Free cash flow 1 was $1.1 billion, with trailing twelve-month cash flow conversion 1 of 84%. • Returns to shareholders totaled $253 million of dividends in the quarter. CEO QUOTE “Dow delivered a solid third quarter, driven by targeted downstream growth and disciplined execution against an evolving macro backdrop,” said Karen S. Carter, Dow chief executive officer. “Our teams are delivering on our unique-to-Dow self-help commitments – including our 2025 $1 billion cost program, our European asset actions, and Transform to Outperform. Specific to the transformation, we are on track to achieve the upsized $700 million in growth and productivity benefits in 2026, as well as the approximately $2 billion in total uplift by the end of next year. In addition, we captured sequential gains from the first of our three European asset shutdowns, where the total benefits are expected to build through 2027. We also remain focused on cash, including releasing more than $400 million of working capital during the quarter and reducing debt by approximately $600 million year-to-date. Our near-term actions are building a Dow that delivers stronger, more consistent results and long-term value for our shareholders.” SUMMARY FINANCIAL RESULTS Three Months Ended Sep 30 In millions, except per share amounts 3Q26 3Q25 vs. SQLY [B / (W)] Net Sales $ 11,267 $ 9,973 $ 1,294 GAAP Income, Net of Tax $ 525 $ 124 $ 401 Op. EBIT $ 585 $ 199 $ 386 Packaging & Specialty Plastics segment net sales in the quarter were $5.8 billion, up 18% versus the year-ago period. Local price increased 17% year-over-year, primarily driven by higher prices across both businesses in EMEAI and the U.S. & Canada. Currency was flat. Volume increased 1% year-over-year, primarily driven by increases in EMEAI in both businesses. Op. EBIT was $585 million, an increase of $386 million compared to the year-ago period, driven by higher integrated margins as a result of higher polyethylene prices and tailwinds from the Company’s self-help initiatives, which were partly offset by higher planned maintenance activity. Packaging and Specialty Plastics business reported a net sales increase versus the year-ago period, driven by higher polyethylene and functional polymers prices in all regions. Polyethylene demand remained resilient, with year-over-year volume growth excluding supply constraints associated with the Middle East conflict. Hydrocarbons & Energy business reported a year-over-year increase in net sales, with higher price and volume for Olefins and Aromatics in EMEAI, enabled by the restart of our previously idled cracker in the region. Industrial Intermediates & Infrastructure Three Months Ended Sep 30 In millions 3Q26 3Q25 vs. SQLY [B / (W)] Net Sales $ 3,058 $ 2,834 $ 224 Op. EBIT $ 176 $ (47) $ 223 Industrial Intermediates & Infrastructure segment net sales in the quarter were $3.1 billion, up 8% versus the year-ago period. Local price increased 16% year-over-year, reflecting gains in both businesses and in all regions. Currency decreased net sales by 1%. Volume decreased 7% year-over-year, as higher volumes in Industrial Solutions were more than offset by lower volumes in Polyurethanes & Construction Chemicals, including impacts from the Middle East conflict in both businesses. Op. EBIT was $176 million, an increase of $223 million versus the year-ago period, driven by higher margins, tailwinds from the Company’s self-help initiatives and the suspension of the recognition of equity losses from Sadara, all of which were partially offset by higher energy costs in EMEAI. Polyurethanes & Construction Chemicals business reported an increase in net sales compared to the year-ago period, primarily driven by local price gains in propylene oxide derivatives in the U.S. & Canada and EMEAI. This was partially offset by lower volumes, which primarily reflect impacts from the Middle East conflict. Industrial Solutions business reported an increase in net sales compared to the year-ago period, driven by local price gains in all regions. Volume growth was driven by increased demand for AI infrastructure and energy applications, as well as higher ethylene oxide project-related catalyst sales. 2 Dow reports third quarter 2026 results Performance Materials & Coatings Three Months Ended Sep 30 In millions 3Q26 3Q25 vs. SQLY [B / (W)] Net Sales $ 2,250 $ 2,082 $ 168 Op. EBIT $ 154 $ 80 $ 74 Performance Materials & Coatings segment net sales in the quarter were $2.3 billion, up 8% versus the year-ago period. Local price increased 5% year-over-year in both businesses, led by Coatings & Performance Monomers. Currency was flat. Volume increased 3% year-over-year, driven by higher volumes in both businesses, led by growth in downstream silicones. Op. EBIT was $154 million, an increase of $74 million versus the year-ago period, driven by tailwinds from the Company’s self-help initiatives, including the closure of the Barry, U.K. siloxanes plant, as well as price and volume gains across both businesses. Consumer Solutions business reported an increase in net sales versus the year-ago period, driven by downstream silicones volume gains in all regions, as growth in consumer, electronics and home care applications more than offset upstream volume declines following the recent shutdown of the Barry, U.K. siloxanes plant. Coatings & Performance Monomers business reported an increase in net sales across all regions compared to the year-ago period, led by higher price and volume in both acrylic monomers and architectural coatings. OUTLOOK “We are building a more resilient and competitive Dow that is positioned to create long-term value through our continued focus on three priorities,” said Carter. “First, driving growth and innovation in higher-value areas of our businesses where demand is growing well above GDP – including applications for AI infrastructure, home and personal care, electronics, flexible packaging and mobility. Second, we are taking action to strengthen the competitiveness of Dow’s portfolio by investing in differentiated low-cost positions while shutting down higher-cost upstream capacity. And third, we’re maintaining a disciplined and balanced approach to capital allocation that supports long-term shareholder value creation. These priorities are underpinned by our self-help actions, which are on track to deliver more than $1 billion of EBITDA uplift in both 2026 and 2027.” Conference Call Dow will host a live webcast of its quarterly earnings conference call with investors to discuss its results, business outlook and other matters today at 8:00 a.m. ET. The webcast and slide presentation that accompany the conference call will be posted on the events and presentations page of investors.dow.com. About Dow Dow (NYSE: DOW) is one of the world’s leading materials science companies, serving customers in high-growth markets such as packaging, infrastructure, mobility and consumer applications. Our global breadth, asset integration and scale, customer-focused innovation and leading business positions enable us to achieve profitable growth and help deliver a sustainable future. We operate manufacturing sites in 29 countries and employed approximately 34,600 people as of year-end 2025. Dow delivered sales of approximately $40 billion in 2025. reference.summary: Dow Inc., through its subsidiaries, provides various materials science solutions for packaging, infrastructure, mobility, and consumer applications in the United States, Canada, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, India, the Asia Pacific, and Latin America. The company operates through Packaging & Specialty Plastics, Industrial Intermediates & Infrastructure, and Performance Materials & Coatings segments. The Packaging & Specialty Plastics segment provides ethylene, propylene, polyethylene, and aromatics products; and other ethylene derivatives, such as polyolefin elastomers, ethylene vinyl acetate, and ethylene propylene diene monomer rubber.
